content.title: About
content.content: Breaded meatballs are small balls made from ground meat (commonly beef, pork, or a blend) that are coated in a crispy breadcrumb crust and served with a savory gravy. They are quick to prepare and work well as a main dish or a convenient snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Meatballs originated in medieval Europe as a way to use leftover meat.
The breadcrumb coating helps retain moisture, keeping the interior juicy.
Traditional gravy is made from stock, cream, and spices, giving a rich flavor.
In Russia, meatballs are often paired with mashed potatoes or pasta.
Variations include chicken, turkey, veal, or even vegetarian versions made from legumes.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The meat provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat contains heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: B12 and B6 support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Zinc present in meat helps maintain a healthy immune response.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of protein and fat makes the dish a good source of sustained energy.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Using fatty ground meat and a thick breadcrumb coating can increase calorie count.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Breadcrumbs contain wheat, which is important for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Meat must be cooked thoroughly to avoid salmonella and other pathogens.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared gravies often contain salt; those monitoring blood pressure should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the hot meatballs drenched in gravy. They pair well with mashed potatoes, rice, pasta, or fresh vegetables. For a lighter option, bake them in the oven instead of frying.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked meatballs in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat until the internal temperature reaches 75 °C.
